Subject: Support coverage and incident communications - IRONBRIDGE RFP QUESTIONS

Vanessa —

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the RFP. A few targeted questions on support/TAM coverage and incident comms so we can finalize the security appendix and SLA exhibit for procurement:

1) Support hours and response expectations: please confirm business-hours and after-hours response SLOs by severity (P1/P2/P3).
2) Escalation ladder: who is the escalation path for after-hours P1 incidents? Do you provide a single-point TAM bridge lead or is it routed through support?
3) Pager/alerting: do you provide PagerDuty contact for infra-impacting events? Is there a 24x7 engineering escalation?
4) Runbooks & evidence: we need a sample incident runbook and the SOC2 section that covers incident detection/response — can you attach a redacted sample?
5) SLA exhibit: confirm whether the SLA includes a guarantee for a mitigation workaround timeframe for Sev1/P1 events or only response/acknowledgement SLAs.
6) Maintenance windows: how are planned maintenance windows communicated and do they factor into uptime calculations?

I've attached the RFI spreadsheet with the priority questions highlighted (ironbridge-rfi-support-questions.xlsx). Can you get us a draft SLA exhibit and TAM roster that we can circulate to our legal and security teams?

We are aiming to complete procurement review by Apr 28.

Thanks,
Maya Singh
Senior Procurement Manager
Ironbridge Bank

Maya —

Appreciate the clarity on the questions. Attaching a draft SLA exhibit (redwood-sla-exhibit-draft.pdf) and a TAM contact roster (tam-contact-roster.csv) for your review. High-level answers up front:

- Business hours support: 08:00–18:00 local business days (US).
- After-hours coverage: 24x7 critical incident monitoring with follow-the-sun TAM escalation (US/EU/APAC); engineering escalation via PagerDuty for P1s.
- Response SLOs (draft): P1 — initial response within 15 minutes; P2 — 1 hour; P3 — 4 business hours. Mitigation target for P1s: best-effort workaround within 4 hours (we can commit this in the SLA exhibit as an objective, or as a guaranteed target for dedicated commitments).
- Maintenance windows: planned maintenance will be communicated 72 hours in advance and do not count against uptime if scheduled; emergency maintenance will be escalated and treated as an incident.
- Runbook sample: attached is a redacted incident runbook excerpt (see section 3) that shows bridge roles and required customer contacts.

Next steps: can we schedule a 30-minute alignment call tomorrow (Apr 22) to walk legal/security through the exhibit and finalize language? I copied Ben and Karthik — Ben will own the SLA wording and Karthik will confirm operational runbook language. Grace (CC on later updates) will be the primary TAM for the account once live.

Best,

Subject: Internal: suggested SLA/esc policy edits for Ironbridge

Vanessa / Karthik / Grace —

Quick internal note after reviewing Maya's list and our draft: proposed language changes we should push back / confirm with the customer before DocuSign:

1) Severity definitions: make P1 = production outage impacting >40% of requests or any data-loss incident requiring immediate mitigation. Keep initial response = 15 minutes and add a "first on-call triage" action item to identify mitigation path within 60 minutes.
2) Escalation path (proposed): TAM -> Redwood Support L2 -> Redwood Engineering on-call (PagerDuty) -> Engineering Manager -> CTO on-call (for cross-region incidents). For after-hours the TAM becomes the bridge coordinator and will remain the single PO for Ironbridge until the incident is resolved.
3) Bridge responsibilities: assign a dedicated bridge coordinator for P1s; coordinator duties include running the incident bridge, triaging, and owning communications to customer stakeholders. We should explicitly call this out under "Incident Roles."
4) Workaround guarantee: for Dedicated/Committed contracts we can guarantee a 4-hour mitigation SLA for P1s; for shared-hosted customers we should position it as a "targeted mitigation timeframe" unless customer signs up for a dedicated capacity addendum.
5) Post-incident evidence: we will provide a postmortem within 72 hours for high-severity incidents and a SOC2 evidence packet upon request (we'll redact customer-specific data).

Please let me know any redlines. Once Vanessa confirms I will prepare the final wording to hand to legal for the SLA exhibit.

Ben Carter
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Maya —

Thanks — quick summary and confirmations to close the thread:

• Workaround guarantee: For Ironbridge (pending deal and a reserved capacity addendum), Redwood will include a contractual 4-hour mitigation guarantee for P1 incidents in the SLA exhibit. For hosted/shared customers this remains a targeted operational objective.

• Bridge coordinator and engineering presence: confirmed. For P1s we will assign a named bridge coordinator (TAM-led) and ensure the Redwood Engineering on-call is paged and remains on-bridge until customer authorizes handoff. That is called out in section 2.1 of the attached final SLA exhibit (redwood-sla-exhibit-final.pdf).

• Maintenance windows: scheduled maintenance will be posted to the customer events calendar and will be excluded from uptime calculations if scheduled 72 hours in advance. Emergency maintenance that impacts availability will be treated as an incident with a post-incident summary and remediation plan.

• Onboarding kick-off: we can begin a soft onboarding (TAM introduction, pre-kickoff checklist) prior to signed DocuSign, but production cutovers and SLA-backed commitments begin after the executed agreement.
